title: For months, OpenAI’s agent swarms have been attacking online databases to find obscure facts
slides: OpenAI's agent swarms: dark side of automation?
They probe online databases for hidden data.
Goal: find obscure facts, not to exploit.
This speeds drug discovery and fact-checking.
Ask: should AI scan your data?
thread_text:
1. AI Agents Are Scanning Your Data

OpenAI's agent swarms are probing online databases right now, hunting for hidden information you never meant to share.

2. The Goal Isn't Exploitation

They're built to find obscure facts, not to steal or hack. That distinction matters more than you think.

3. Faster Cures, Quicker Checks

This same tech could slash drug discovery timelines and fact-check claims in seconds instead of days.

4. But Who Controls the Swarm?

If these agents can dig up anything, the real question is who decides what's fair game.

5. Should AI Scan Your Data?

Open your settings on any app you use daily. Check if your data is opt-in or opt-out. Does it make sense to let an AI scan it?

instagram.caption:
Software agents are scanning online databases right now, hunting for hidden facts nobody meant to surface.

OpenAI built these agent swarms to dig up obscure information, and the stated goal isn't hacking or theft.

That same tech could cut drug discovery timelines and fact-check claims in seconds instead of days. 🔍

But if an agent can pull up anything, someone has to decide what's fair game — and right now, that someone isn't you. ⚖️

For anyone who publishes or stores data, the question shifts from "is it public" to "did I consent to this scan." 🗂️

Open your settings on the apps you use daily. Is your data opt-in or opt-out? 🧩

Would you let an AI read it?
